title: Unroll a circle
hook: Why does a circle's area have a radius squared in it? Slice it and lay it flat.

knows: the rim (circumference) of a circle is pi times its diameter
the area of a rectangle is width times height
doesNotKnow: why the circle area formula has a radius squared

misconception: A circle fills about as much as the square around it, or its area formula is arbitrary.
objective: The learner can explain that a circle cut into many thin slices rearranges into a near-rectangle r tall and half the circumference (pi r) long, so its area is pi r^2, which is about 78.5% of the surrounding square.

claims.text: A circle of radius 10 has area about 314, which is about 78% (78.5%) of its 20 x 20 square of area 400.
Half the rim of a circle of radius 10 is pi x 10, about 31.4.
claims.source: Circumference = 2 pi r (definition of pi as circumference over diameter); half is pi r = 31.42.

claims.text: Equal slices laid alternately point-up and point-down form a strip about r tall and pi r long; more slices straighten its edges without changing its area, so the circle's area is pi r x r = pi r^2.
claims.source: N wedges of half-angle pi/N: strip centre-line length N r sin(pi/N) -> pi r and height r cos(pi/N) -> r as N grows; rearrangement preserves area. Standard limit argument; e.g. Strogatz, Infinite Powers (2019), ch. 1.

claims.text: Any circle fills pi / 4, about 78.5%, of the square drawn around it.

recall.question: A round table of radius 1 m just fits inside a 2 m x 2 m square rug, touching all four edges. Roughly how much of the rug does the table cover?
recall.why: Unrolled, the table is a strip 1 m tall and half its rim (pi x 1, about 3.14 m) long: about 3.14 of the 4 square metres.
